title: Looking up and disputing a URL's category: URL Lookup and Site Review

prose.text: Two tools show how Zscaler categorizes a site. {{url-lookup-console}} {{ip-categorized-example}}

prose.label: Disputing a category.
prose.text: {{reclassification-request}} Turnaround beyond best effort is open {{gap:site-review-turnaround}}.

url-lookup-console.statement: In the Zscaler Admin Console, an admin can see how Zscaler categorizes a site according to its URL or IP address. The result shows the URL Classifications (the predefined category or super category of the URL), the Security Alert associated with the URL, and the Cloud Application category and cloud application the URL is associated with.

quotes: In the Zscaler Admin Console, you have the ability to see how Zscaler categorizes a site according to its URL or IP address.
URL Classifications: The predefined category or super category of the URL.
Security Alert: The security alert associated with the URL.
Cloud Application: The cloud application category and cloud application with which the URL is associated.

ip-categorized-example.statement: If a SaaS or cloud provider dedicates an IP address or IP range to an application, the Zscaler service categorizes it. The page's example: 13.107.6.152/31 is used for Microsoft 365 and is categorized as Professional Services and Microsoft 365.

quotes: However, if a SaaS or cloud provider dedicates an IP address or IP range to an application, the Zscaler service categorizes it.
For example, 13.107.6.152/31 is used for Microsoft 365 and is categorized as Professional Services and Microsoft 365.

site-review-tool.statement: Site Review is a URL categorization lookup tool that can be accessed by users going through the Zscaler service, at https://sitereview.zscaler.com/. Its results might vary from those seen in the tenant's environment due to custom categories that the admin has configured.

quotes: Site Review is a URL categorization lookup tool that can be accessed by users going through the Zscaler service.
Results might vary from those seen in your environment due to custom categories that your admin has configured.

site-review-input.statement: Site Review accepts up to three sites per lookup. The URL or IP address is automatically populated in the Enter URL field when a review is requested from the blocked EUN page. A request can select up to three categories that seem appropriate for the website.

quotes: Press Enter on your keyboard or click Add More to add up to three sites.
The URL or IP address is automatically populated in the Enter URL field when you request a review of it from the blocked EUN page.
Select up to three categories that you think are appropriate for the website.

site-review-languages.statement: The Site Review website supports Chinese, Chinese Taiwan (Optional), English (United States), English (United Kingdom), French, German, Japanese, Russian and Spanish, and the browser language settings must be set to one of them.

quotes: The Site Review website supports multiple languages (i.e., Chinese, Chinese Taiwan (Optional), English (United States), English (United Kingdom), French, German, Japanese, Russian, and Spanish).
Ensure to set the browser language settings to one of the supported languages.

reclassification-request.statement: A site the user thinks is incorrectly categorized can be sent through Site Review to request reclassification. A Support case is automatically created for each request based on the requester's email address, and an email notification follows the review. Requests are handled on a best-effort basis and are not covered by an SLA. Site Review does not allow recategorization of a URL to a specific cloud application; to do that, contact Zscaler Support.

quotes: If you think that a website is incorrectly categorized, you can also use Site Review to request reclassification. For each request, based on your email address, a Support case is automatically created.
After the request is reviewed, you get an email notification.
Site Review requests are handled on a best-effort basis. The requests submitted through the Site Review website aren’t covered by an SLA.
The site review website doesn't allow recategorization of a URL to a specific cloud application
To recategorize a URL to a specific cloud application, contact Zscaler Support.

site-review-turnaround.title: How long a Site Review reclassification takes
site-review-turnaround.detail: The page says requests are handled on a best-effort basis with no SLA and gives no turnaround time.
